title: Flyers’ Noah Cates out for remainder of series against Hurricanes with lower-body injury
content:
VOORHEES TOWNSHIP, N.J. — Flyers center Noah Cates will miss the remainder of Philadelphia’s second-round Stanley Cup playoff series against the Carolina Hurricanes with a lower-body injury, coach Rick Tocchet said Wednesday.

In eight playoff games, the 27-year-old Cates has one goal, three assists and a minus-2 rating. Cates, primarily the Flyers’ third-line center, played in all 82 regular-season games and set career highs in goals (18), assists (29) and points (47). He led the Flyers with a plus-26 rating.

The Hurricanes lead the best-of-seven series 2-0. Game 3 is at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Thursday night.

“These are bumps in the road we’re going to have to deal with,” Tocchet said, “but there’s opportunity for guys.”

The Flyers’ four centers for Game 3 figure to be Trevor Zegras, Christian Dvorak, Sean Couturier and Denver Barkey. Dvorak missed Wednesday’s practice and is day to day with an undisclosed injury, but Tocchet suggested he’ll be fine for the game.

Zegras, who played wing for most of the regular season, was shifted to center in early March after the trade deadline. Tocchet moved him back to left wing midway through Game 1 and kept him there for Game 2.

Barkey started Game 2 in the middle of Alex Bump and Porter Martone, after Tocchet moved him there midway through Game 1. Other than in the regular-season finale — when Tocchet decided to give Barkey a look at center after a suggestion from Flyers president of hockey operations Keith Jones — the 21-year-old rookie played exclusively on the wing after he was recalled in December.

Tocchet reiterated Wednesday that he’s intrigued by Barkey’s versatility.

“He’s a pretty smart kid,” Tocchet said. “I’ve used him (at center) twice now in a hostile environment, so I think that should give him confidence. Today he was smiling, having (fun). He’s welcomed this situation to play center for us. We’re going to need him. He’s going to get some ice time now that Catesy’s out.”

The Flyers recalled center prospect Jett Luchanko from his junior club in Brantford on Wednesday, but Tocchet indicated that Luchanko would only play if there are further injuries.

Flyers winger Owen Tippett, who has missed the first two games of the series, took part in Wednesday’s practice. He’s a game-time decision for Game 3.
